The test image shows split soybean stems with distinctly brown/reddish-brown internal pith tissue. This is a stem cross-section showing internal discoloration. Key observations:
- Stems split lengthwise showing brown pith
- Brown discoloration throughout the internal tissue
- Hairy stem surface typical of soybean

Top candidate: **Brown_Stem_Rot** — the hallmark diagnostic is brown pith when stem is split. SDS would show white pith. Let me confirm with one reference image.

The reference image for Brown_Stem_Rot shows stems split to reveal white/healthy pith (for comparison), while the test image shows clearly brown/reddish-brown pith throughout the split stems. This brown pith discoloration is the definitive diagnostic sign of Brown Stem Rot. SDS would show white pith when cut, which eliminates that possibility.
